key_points: Before becoming vice president and later president, Joe Biden served 36 years in the U.S. Senate representing Delaware, commuting daily by train to be home with his sons after his first wife and daughter died in a 1972 car accident.
Biden served two terms as vice president under Barack Obama and is considered one of the most influential vice presidents in U.S. history.
After his son Beau died of brain cancer in 2015, Biden decided not to run for president in 2016, but he later launched a successful campaign in 2019-2020.
Biden defeated Donald Trump in the 2020 election with a record number of votes, though Trump rejected the results, and Biden was sworn in as president on January 20, 2021, calling for national unity.
main_idea: The passage traces Joe Biden's life before his presidency, from personal tragedies and decades in the Senate to his role as vice president and his path to winning the 2020 presidential election.
restate_sentence: He briefly considered leaving his Senate seat.
